report.summary: The release expands editor inspection and selection tools while improving storage-size handling.
keyChanges: Opening the context menu on empty canvas adds an option to show or hide the Stats panel, which reports scene element count and dimensions, storage sizes, and applicable selected-element details.
The panel shows details for one selected or edited element, including its angle, and shows count and combined dimensions for multiple selected elements.

The total browser-storage size still counts the saved drawing, app state, collaboration data, and library using the same calculation; the drawing-size calculation has been extracted without an evidenced change in results.
Debounced actions now expose a cancellation option, but no supplied caller uses it, so no user-visible effect is established.
The singular selection-target helper is removed and the scene export uses a plural name, but the evidence does not show the replacement behavior or confirm what selection controls now do.
Appearance controls and sharpness settings now consider the full selection rather than a single target, so mixed selections may expose controls or update defaults differently.

The new Stats panel code reports scene and selection properties, including element count, bounds, and storage sizes; the statistics display state defaults to off and is retained when clearing the canvas.
qaChecks: Verify that opening the context menu on empty canvas offers the Stats panel, and choosing it displays the scene element count and dimensions.
Check that with exactly one element selected, the panel shows its position, width, height, and angle; with exactly two selected, it shows the selected count and combined dimensions.
Confirm that the panel shows scene and total storage sizes after the size calculation updates, and that its close control hides the panel.

Check whether the selection and shape-property controls still behave correctly when an element is being edited while multiple shapes are selected; the expected behavior after this change is not established by the supplied evidence.
Verify the mixed selection exposes the sharpness control when at least one selected element supports sharpness.
Check that applying a sharpness value updates the selected elements and that a mixed selection does not change the default sharpness for newly drawn elements.
Confirm the Stats panel reports the scene element count and dimensions, and reports selected-element properties when elements are selected.
Verify that clearing the canvas retains the Stats panel’s previously enabled state; the panel should remain open if it was open before the clear.
uncertainty: The supplied changes add the Stats feature and make selection helpers formatting-only edits, so no concrete input that behaved differently before and after can be established.
The replacement selection-target behavior is not shown, so the exact input that now follows a different path and the expected outcome for selection controls cannot be determined.

The prior single-target selection rule is not supplied, so the exact multi-selection cases that differ from the previous behavior cannot be confirmed; no application navigation or render relationship for opening the Stats panel is supplied.

report.summary: The release expands interactive console experiences with configurable prompts and clearer feedback.
keyChanges: Browser console instances now support prompts: confirm prompts use the browser confirmation dialog, while other prompt types use a text prompt and do not apply their configured choices, placeholder, or initial value.

The console prompt method now delegates to its configured prompt handler and throws an error when no handler is configured; the added example demonstrates text, confirmation, selection, and optional multi-selection prompts.
Confirmation prompts default to Yes and No with Yes initially selected unless an initial answer is supplied, and show the chosen answer when completed or cancelled.
Single-choice, multi-choice, and grouped choice prompts display option labels, hints, selection states, and submitted choices.
Text prompts show a placeholder for an empty value and display entered text or validation errors according to the prompt state.

Console instances accept caller-supplied options, including reporter lists, while retaining the environment-based default reporter when no reporter list is supplied; callers can now intentionally create an instance with no reporters.
Console instances now expose prompts for text, confirmation, single selection, and multiple selection, including defaults, placeholders, initial values, and optional selection requirements.
The shared entry point no longer exports the instance factory, while the main entry point defines and exports it.
Status messages now use distinct markers and format multiline text with continuation bars, while an empty message prints only the bar.
The key-choice prompt renders the active option, the submitted choice, or the first option as cancelled.
The progress indicator removes one to three trailing periods from its starting message and replaces the animation with a completion message when stopped.
Password prompts support validation and a configurable mask, with separate displays for active, submitted, canceled, and error states.
Grouped prompts run in order; when a prompt is canceled and a cancellation callback is supplied, its result is recorded as “canceled,” the callback runs, and the group continues.
Message notes remove recognized ANSI escape sequences when calculating line widths, and prompt symbols select Unicode or fallback characters according to terminal support.

Check a text prompt configured with initial value "java" and placeholder "Not sure"; confirm the browser text prompt is shown without applying those settings.

Test a select prompt with options "TypeScript", "TypeScript", and "CoffeeScript", then a multiselect prompt with ESLint, Prettier, and GitHub Action; confirm each uses a text prompt rather than presenting the configured choices.

Check a required multi-choice prompt with zero options selected and press Enter; confirm it displays the message asking for at least one selection rather than submitting.
Verify a text prompt with an empty value displays its configured placeholder, then enter text and confirm the submitted prompt displays that text.
Confirm single-choice and grouped choice prompts display their option labels and hints while active, show selection states, and display chosen labels after submission.
Verify creating an instance with reporters set to an empty array and logging a message produces no reporter output; previously, that argument was ignored and the default reporter was used.
Check that the main entry point still exposes the instance factory and the shared entry point no longer exposes it.
Verify a confirmation prompt with initial set to false starts on No and returns false when submitted without changing the selection.
Check a multiple-selection prompt with options ["A"] and required set to false; submit without selecting anything and confirm it accepts the empty selection.
Verify status output for the exact empty message "" prints only the bar and a newline.
Check status output for the exact message "First\nSecond" places the first line after its status marker and prefixes the second line with a continuation bar.
Confirm a two-option prompt shows the active option, then shows the selected option after submission; when cancelled, confirm the first option is shown as cancelled.
Test a progress message of "Loading..." and confirm the starting display uses "Loading"; after stopping with "Done", confirm the animation is cleared and the completion message appears.
Verify a password prompt using a custom mask displays masked input and its validation error when validation rejects the entered value.
Check a grouped prompt where the first prompt is canceled and an on-cancel callback is supplied: confirm the callback receives that prompt's result as “canceled” and the next prompt still runs.
Confirm a note containing ANSI escape sequences is printed with its message text and does not count those sequences toward its displayed line width.
uncertainty: The prompt capability is newly added, so the supplied evidence does not establish a concrete input handled by the old behavior that changes path in the new behavior.
No prior implementation is included in the supplied changes, so a concrete input that behaved differently before this change cannot be established.
The prompt capability is new in this change, so the evidence provides no prior behavior or input for comparison to identify a regression-triggering case.

The supplied changes contain no removed code or documented prior behavior, so the exact input that the old behavior handled differently cannot be identified; regression checks for the rendering and prompt changes cannot be based on a verified before-and-after difference.

report.summary: The release improves how the whiteboard edits, updates, and restores drawing scenes, including when loading imported or saved content.
keyChanges: Selection and element-ordering actions now return the updated elements for callers that assign their results, allowing the editor to retain changes from selection-box gestures, deletion, and layer reordering.
Undo and redo now return restored scene snapshots instead of modifying the existing scene array, and invalid serialized history entries return no snapshot rather than throwing.
Clearing selection now returns a shallow copy of the scene array while deselecting its elements; the supplied code shows no resulting visible change to normal editing.
Deleting selected elements now applies the filtered drawing, so selected objects should disappear instead of remaining visible.
Undo and redo now apply a returned drawing when one is available, and startup loads saved drawing elements separately from app state, including a refresh when app state is absent.
Pasted drawings are no longer normalized by subtracting their minimum x and y coordinates, so drawings copied from nonzero coordinates can appear offset from their former placement.
Clicking an unselected object that overlaps a selected object can now leave both selected, rather than clearing the previous selection first.
Cutting selected objects now uses the deletion result, and scene loading now replaces the current elements with the loaded elements.
Text editing removes every canvas object with the clicked text object's ID, rather than removing only that specific object; duplicate IDs can therefore affect other objects.
The editor accepts read-only element collections at the type level; drawing behavior is unchanged.

Importing malformed JSON now produces an empty scene instead of letting JSON parsing fail; a valid JSON file with no elements also produces an empty scene, whereas previously it left the current elements unchanged.
When saved elements are valid but saved app-state data is malformed, restoration now preserves the drawing instead of discarding its elements.

Check deleting a selected element, then cutting a selected element, removes the selected element while leaving unselected elements in the drawing.
Confirm moving a selected element one layer forward and backward changes its overlap order while preserving the drawing.
Test moving selected elements to the front and back, including selecting more than one element, and confirm the selected elements change order while remaining in the drawing.
Verify selecting one or more elements and pressing Delete or Backspace removes them from the drawing.
Check that pressing the platform command key plus Z after an undoable edit restores the prior drawing, and pressing Shift with that shortcut reapplies the edit.
Confirm that opening the editor with saved drawing data but no saved app-state data displays the saved drawing.
Verify that when Undo or Redo encounters a malformed serialized history entry, the current drawing remains unchanged and the editor remains usable.
Verify pasting the drawing with minimum coordinates x=100 and y=50 places it 100 units farther right and 50 units farther down than the former normalized placement.
Check that clicking an unselected object overlapping a selected object leaves both objects selected.
Confirm cutting a selected object removes it from the canvas and places its selected drawing data on the clipboard.
Validate loading the prepared scene replaces the existing canvas contents with the loaded elements.
Test editing one of the two pasted text objects with the shared ID and verify the other text object remains after editing.
Confirm that no runtime behavior change is expected from this group.
Verify importing malformed JSON results in an empty scene rather than failing during JSON parsing.
Check importing a valid JSON file with no elements clears the current drawing; previously, this input left the current elements unchanged.
Verify reopening the editor with valid saved elements and malformed saved app-state data keeps the saved drawing available.
uncertainty: Malformed serialized history is the only input shown to take a different runtime path, but no supplied application workflow can create or inject it.
The previous scene-loading helper contract is not supplied, so the exact input that makes the old and new loading paths differ cannot be determined.
No concrete input takes a different runtime path before and after these changes because the supplied changes only affect collection typing and equivalent empty-array initialization.
It is unclear whether importing a valid JSON file with no elements is intended to clear the current drawing or leave it unchanged.

report.summary: The release makes text rendering and placement more consistent across editing and drawing workflows.
keyChanges: Text dimensions are now calculated from canvas-measured line widths and a line-height estimate of 1.2 times the font size, rather than browser-rendered dimensions; text size and position may differ when created, edited, or resized.

Bound text is wrapped before its dimensions are measured instead of being measured with a container-width limit, and a word exactly as wide as the available line is now kept intact rather than entering the over-width word-breaking path.
Text measurement now normalizes carriage-return line endings, so pasted text containing CRLF or lone-CR breaks is measured as separate lines without treating the carriage return as part of a line.
New text created without a parent-centering position is no longer shifted upward by half its baseline, changing where it appears relative to the click.

Canvas and SVG text rendering now position lines from the bottom of each line instead of using the stored baseline and the prior bottom-alignment offset; detached and restored text is rendered using this updated layout.
Resizing text and elements with attached text now scales font size from width and no longer recalculates the text baseline, which can change alignment after height-changing transformations.
Editing text attached to a shape now measures and updates its editor size even for a single line; Firefox and Safari also receive a 0.5-pixel editor-width adjustment.
qaChecks: Verify that text containing “alpha” followed by a CRLF and “beta” displays as two lines, with no stray carriage-return spacing and dimensions consistent with those lines.
Check that a single word exactly matching the bound-text usable width remains on one line rather than being split or producing an extra line.
Confirm that editing multiline text at 20 px produces a height based on approximately 24 px per line and that centered, unbound text remains positioned around its center as its text changes.
Ensure that restored text retains its line breaks and that bound text is wrapped to its container without clipping or unexpected extra lines.
Verify creating text on a blank canvas at a chosen point places it from that point without the previous upward baseline shift.
Check that multi-line text bound to a container with bottom vertical alignment is positioned using the updated line-bottom layout.
Confirm that detaching text from a shape or arrow leaves readable standalone text with its measured dimensions.
Verify importing the drawing restores readable text and that the stored baseline does not determine its rendered position.
Check that image and SVG exports render multi-line bottom-aligned bound text using the updated line-bottom positioning.
Verify that resizing attached text or its shape vertically, without changing its width, keeps the text legible and aligned in its container.
Check that changing an arrow endpoint keeps its attached label positioned and legible, and that horizontally or vertically flipping an element with attached text leaves the text legible.
Verify that editing a single-line label, the case previously excluded from automatic editor resizing, keeps the text visible and the editor aligned with the shape.
Check a label that wraps within a narrow shape in Firefox and Safari; confirm the editor remains aligned and the wrapped text stays visible.
uncertainty: The new line-height estimate and canvas-based width measurement may produce different exact text bounds depending on font and browser; the supplied evidence gives no expected tolerance.

report.summary: The release changes how shared libraries and editor workflows are managed and experienced.
keyChanges: A library link in the URL hash or the legacy query string now imports and merges its items, removes the import parameter from the address, and opens the Library menu; a token matching the editor ID suppresses the import prompt.
Library items are loaded from local storage when the editor starts and refreshed separately when newer browser-tab data is synchronized, rather than being included with scene updates.
The embeddable editor API now exposes library updates instead of the previous library-import method, changing the integration contract for developers.
Loading a library file now merges its unique items with the existing Library and opens the Library menu.
The embedded editor now exposes a library-update operation that replaces existing items by default unless merging is requested; scene updates no longer apply supplied library items.
The editor’s former startup URL import path was removed, but supplied evidence does not establish whether the new library URL handling preserves that flow.

Importing a valid Library file now adds its items to the Library and opens the Library menu instead of passing the file contents through the scene update, so the current drawing should not be replaced by the Library contents.
Pointer updates now show x and y values in the example, initially displaying 0 for each coordinate until pointer data arrives.
Comment tools and drawing operations now use the editor API; their existing visible workflows should remain usable.
qaChecks: Verify that opening a library-import link with the library URL in the query string imports and merges its items, removes the import parameter from the address, and opens the Library menu; this query-string input distinguishes the new behavior from the previous hash-only handling.
Check that a hash-format library link with a token matching the editor ID imports without a prompt, while a link with a nonmatching token prompts before import.
Confirm that changing the hash to a library-import link imports the library and restores the previous address, while a hash change without a library link continues to load the scene.
Verify that the embedded editor exposes the library-update capability and that an initial library source populates the Library when the editor starts.
Check that after newer browser-tab data is synchronized, the Library reflects the stored library items without replacing the drawing scene.
Verify that a startup link with a valid library URL in either supported parameter form prompts for confirmation and, after confirmation, adds the library items.
Verify that dropping a valid library file retains the existing item, adds the distinct imported item, and opens the Library menu.
Check that importing a valid library JSON file adds its distinct item without removing the existing Library item.
Verify that updating the Library with one distinct incoming item and no merge option leaves only the incoming item in the Library.
Check that sending a nonempty library-items list through a scene update does not change the Library, while updating the Library through its dedicated operation does.
Verify importing the valid Library file adds its items to the Library and opens the Library menu without replacing the current drawing.
Check that moving the pointer updates the displayed x and y values, and that before a pointer update both values display as 0.
Confirm the comment tool creates a comment on the drawing and that dragging an existing comment icon moves it.
Ensure resetting the scene and using the canvas, PNG, and SVG export actions still work with the current drawing.
uncertainty: The diff does not establish a user-visible difference for library restoration from local storage versus scene loading, so a specific regression-triggering input for that change cannot be identified.
The removed startup URL importer may have been replaced by new library URL handling; the supplied evidence does not show whether links still prompt and import items.
The previous browser hash-change listener was removed, but the supplied evidence does not establish what response to a hash change the example is expected to provide.

report.summary: Arrow editing is refined to make selecting, connecting, and adjusting arrow attachments more consistent and interactive.
keyChanges: Moving only an interior point on a multi-point arrow now recalculates its bound endpoints, so connected shapes remain attached as the route changes.
Dragging an arrow focus point now updates both bound ends and their connection modes, so changes to an arrow connection can reposition its other endpoint too.
Arrow connection geometry now uses a calculated element center, and rectangular corner points are no longer automatically shifted away from the selected point.

Arrow targeting now uses a zoom-adjusted distance value directly, and the opposite endpoint is checked with the canvas hit test; this can change which nearby shapes arrows and elbow arrows connect to.

When a selected arrow has two points, binding is enabled, and a bound focus point is visible on its shape, the canvas now shows a focus-point circle and dashed connection; hovering and pressing near that point identifies it for interaction.
While a selected linear element is actively being dragged, its ordinary hovered-point highlight is no longer drawn.

Dragging an arrow focus point over a bindable shape attaches the endpoint, while dragging it away moves the endpoint and removes its binding; Alt switches an existing connection between orbit and inside modes.
When several bindable shapes qualify under a focus point, the frontmost qualifying shape is chosen, and releasing the pointer updates the shapes’ recorded arrow connections.
A focus point can be grabbed by clicking it directly, even without a preceding pointer-move event.
Hovering over a focus point on a bound arrow now changes the cursor to a pointer, making that point an interactive target.
Alt key handling now invokes point-drag handling while binding is disabled or re-enabled, affecting editing of arrow focus points.

report.summary: The release improves editor interactions, content generation, and overall usability.
keyChanges: Selection boxes now consider an element’s outline thickness and attached arrow text, and can test outline intersections when overlap mode is used; selection and frame membership may differ near these visible bounds.
Pointer hit-testing now checks a rotated element’s actual bounds rather than its larger unrotated bounding rectangle, so clicks near rotated corners can target differently.
Free-draw elements now use their absolute geometry when calculating their center, which feeds arrow binding and other geometry-based interactions.

New editor state defaults box selection to contain, keeps the preference in browser state, and restores a supplied preference from a scene or local state; this affects the selection mode after opening or reloading a drawing.
Frame-specific image exports now evaluate element overlap using the full drawing’s element map, affecting which content is included in an exported frame.
Multi-element hit detection extends by two transform-handle spacings beyond the previous hit area, making that added margin eligible for moving the selection and showing a move cursor.

Alt plus Ctrl or Command now starts lasso selection even when the pointer is over a selected element or the shared selection bounds, unless a resize handle is active; an existing lasso trail is not restarted.
Frame-based generation and frame-only exports now select elements by intersecting bounds while excluding elements assigned to another frame, so the chosen contents may differ at frame boundaries.
Drag selection now passes the active box-selection setting into element selection, and the browser build preloads the Assistant semibold font.
Preferences now include a box-selection choice between contain and overlap, with the selected option reflected in the editor setting.
Radio menu rows can show an optional icon and truncate labels that exceed available space, affecting the box-selection and theme choice rows.
qaChecks: Verify that a box-selection boundary matching the shape’s geometric bounds but not covering its full outline does not select the shape.
Check that a selection box enclosing an arrow and its attached text includes both visible parts in the selection result.
Verify that clicking inside the rotated rectangle’s unrotated bounding-box corner, but outside the visible rotated rectangle, does not select the rectangle.
Confirm that an arrow can connect to the free-draw element and that its endpoint remains positioned on the element when the drawing is edited.
Verify that opening a scene without a box-selection preference uses contain mode, selecting fully enclosed elements but not elements that only cross the selection boundary.
Confirm that opening a scene with the overlap preference retains that mode, allowing a selection box to include elements that cross its boundary.
Verify that exporting the specific frame includes elements whose bounds overlap it and excludes elements assigned to a different frame, even when they overlap geometrically.
Verify that hovering in the added margin between the previous hit area and the expanded selection bounds shows a move cursor, and that dragging there moves the selection.
Check that Alt plus Ctrl or Command, without a resize handle active, starts lasso selection when dragging from over a selected element or the shared selection bounds.
Confirm that a drag-selection gesture with box-selection mode active selects elements according to that mode.
Verify that frame-only export includes an element whose bounds intersect the frame, excludes an element assigned to another frame, and excludes an element whose bounds only touch the frame edge.
Check that Magic Frame generation uses intersecting elements from its own frame and does not include an element assigned to a different frame.
Verify that Assistant semibold text loads in its intended typeface during editor startup without a visible fallback-to-final-font swap.
Verify choosing contain and then overlap updates which box-selection option is visibly selected.
Check that a menu label exceeding the available width is truncated with an ellipsis and that its radio choices remain available.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not establish whether users can choose overlap box-selection mode, so its outline-intersection behavior has no confirmed manual entry point.

report.summary: The release adds and reorganizes URL handling, including parsing, assembly, encoding, and query parameters.
keyChanges: URL parsing decodes URL components, keeps malformed percent-encoded text unchanged, and represents repeated query keys as arrays when the earlier value is nonempty.
URL composition helpers add or remove a single leading or trailing slash, and an absolute URL with no trailing slash receives an empty path while the same URL with a trailing slash retains “/”.
Query encoding distinguishes a literal plus sign from a space, encoding them as “%2B” and “+” respectively.
Host, path, query, and full URL generation apply encoding rules to their respective components, so spaces and reserved characters can appear differently in generated URL strings.
Query generation omits the equals sign when a scalar value is empty, while array values produce one key-value entry per element; this affects the exact search string produced.
URL inputs can be parsed and formatted as strings, with utilities for retrieving and adding query parameters.
URL composition joins relative paths, combines parameters, carries over a supplied fragment, and rejects appended URLs that have a protocol.
URL credentials are percent-encoded when formatted, and a URL is treated as having a protocol when its parsed protocol is non-empty.
Repeated query keys now produce an array of values instead of keeping only the last value, so callers receive different results for URLs with duplicate keys.

URL parsing, normalization, parameter updates, and joining now use string-based utilities; the former parsed-object input and optional base-stripping behavior are no longer present in the replacement utilities.
A new URL helper collapses repeated slashes in URL text while preserving the protocol delimiter.
Absolute URL output combines the protocol, credentials, host, and full path when a protocol is present and the path is absolute; otherwise it returns only the full path.
Query parameters are exposed with array values as repeated entries, and JSON serialization produces the URL string.

Check parsing ?tag=&tag=blue and confirm the resulting tag value is “blue”; the supplied implementation treats an empty first value as unset when processing a repeated key.

report.summary: The release reshapes URL and query handling, changing how URLs are created, parsed, and serialized while leaving compatibility and some prior behavior uncertain.
keyChanges: Relative inputs now parse as paths, and URL parsing preserves the raw query string for query extraction and URL construction.
Protocol recognition now requires a word-character scheme, so a hyphenated scheme that the previous parser recognized is treated as path text instead.
Query serialization emits falsy values such as 0 as a bare key, while query updates merge supplied values over existing ones and rebuild the URL.
The package entry point now exports URL, query, and encoding modules instead of the prior URL-object module, changing the public capabilities available to consumers.
The search-parameter encoder is removed; previously, an empty value produced a bare key, while arrays produced repeated key-value pairs.
The prior URL object's JSON and string conversion methods are removed, while the new URL type provides JSON serialization as its href.
The previous parameter-reading and parameter-merging helpers are removed as the utility layer shifts to URL-oriented query helpers.
URL construction and relative-path appending are removed; callers can no longer rely on this implementation to parse URLs, merge parameters, or reject appends containing a protocol.
The URL component accessors and query-string conversions are removed, including access to credentials, host, origin, full URL, and repeated query parameters.
URL composition merges query values, joins a nonempty path, replaces the hash when supplied, and rejects an appended URL that has a protocol; resolution uses this composition behavior.

URL string output combines encoded path, query, hash, and—when applicable—protocol, credentials, and host, while URL creation now returns the new URL representation used by normalization and resolution.
The added query types and imports do not change observable behavior, so no application checks are indicated.
qaChecks: Verify parsing /items?x=1 retains /items as the path and exposes x=1 as its query; this relative input previously reached a parser path that could throw.
Check custom-scheme://host/path is treated as path text rather than a URL with a protocol, and confirm whether that result is intended because the previous parser recognized this scheme.
Confirm serializing or adding the query value 0 produces a bare key such as count, without an equals sign or value.
Validate adding y=2 to https://example.test/items?x=1#part preserves the existing x=1, adds y=2, and retains the path and fragment.
Verify that the package entry point exposes the URL, query, encoding, and utility modules and no longer exposes the prior URL-object module.

Confirm that JSON serialization of a URL object returns its href string.
Verify empty-string input: the previous constructor accepted it as an empty URL, and confirm whether an equivalent supported result remains after this removal.
Check appending /child to /base and appending https://other.test/x: the previous behavior joined the relative path and rejected the protocol-bearing URL; confirm the supported behavior now.
Confirm parsing https://user:pass@example.test:8443/a?x=1#part still provides the corresponding URL components through any supported replacement.
